_source: RFC 8448 "Example Handshake Traces for TLS 1.3" (informational, published test vectors) — Section 3, Simple 1-RTT Handshake trace. client_random taken from the ClientHello's raw 'payload (196 octets)' hex dump (bytes 6..38, after the 2-byte legacy_version). client_traffic_secret_0 is the 'expanded' value from the '{client} derive secret "tls13 c ap traffic"' step, restated as the PRK in the immediately-following '{client} derive write traffic keys for application data' step. encrypted_record/expected_plaintext are the first client application_data record sent under that key (sequence number 0), from the '{client} send application_data record' step right after the client Finished message. expected_key/expected_iv are RFC 8448's own derived values for that same step, included here as an independent cross-check on this crate's HKDF-Expand-Label implementation, not read by the Rust test directly.
